title: PRD v2026 ten-item rubric
description: Runtime panel critic for the #prd document and its deck projection. Scores the ten items from one to five; a one on items two, six or eight withholds the artifact; every item must score three or higher for the artifact to ship. Deterministic prechecks run before the scored pass and their failures are reported as item scores, never as prose annotations the reader sees.

anchors.5: An engineer and a designer could start without a clarifying meeting, and an auditor could open every cited source.

two_pass_order: PASS ONE (claims): type every consequential statement per the claim ledger (SUPPORTED_FACT, DERIVATION, DEFENSIBLE_INFERENCE, HYPOTHESIS, EDITORIAL_JUDGMENT, UNKNOWN), scope-match each citation to the sentence it supports, check independence of origins, ignore how the prose sounds.
PASS TWO (prose): slop families, the actor rule, semantic coherence, structure variety, ignore whether claims are true.

rules: every requirement has at least one pain or competitive gap, or is typed HYPOTHESIS and carries a bet
every pain has at least one quote
every quote has exactly one source
every must-have has at least two independent origins
every requirement has at least one acceptance test
every acceptance test and every signal points back to a requirement

deterministic_prechecks.rule: a digit appears only inside verbatim quote text or a typed requirement_target; ids, pointers, standard names and provenance dates are exempt
every signal carries signal, instrument, population, direction, baselineStatus, type and a guardrail with rollback authority; at least one leading and one lagging
the record validates against the PrdAir schema

criteria.label: Thesis
criteria.text: The thesis carries a judgment and names the decision; the titles alone pass the Partner Test.
criteria.five: a partner reading only the title, the thesis and the slide titles understands the argument and the decision asked of them
criteria.one: the thesis is a topic label, names no decision, or the deck titles read as topics

criteria.label: Problem
criteria.text: The problem is a specific story with verbatim named-source quotes from independent origins; no solution appears in the problem.
criteria.five: the story names the user, the need and the insight, and at least two independent source types carry verbatim quotes with pointers
criteria.one: a quote is paraphrased, a source is generic or invented, the quotes trace to one original, or the problem names a feature

criteria.label: Why-Now
criteria.text: Why now is stated and cited.
criteria.five: the named market, regulatory, technology or client change is stated and a cited quote carries it
criteria.one: absent, or a generic urgency sentence with no named change and no quote

criteria.label: Users-And-Jobs
criteria.text: Users are bounded to primary personas with job stories traced to quotes.
criteria.five: one or two primary personas by id with their stage of struggle; every job story is in Klement form and cites its quotes
criteria.one: no primary persona, or job stories without a persona id or a quote

criteria.label: Non-Goals-And-Appetite
criteria.text: Non-goals and appetite are explicit with reasons.
criteria.five: every non-goal carries its reason; the appetite is a typed requirement_target with a qualitative rationale
criteria.one: no non-goals, a non-goal without a reason, or an appetite that is not a typed time budget

criteria.label: Requirements-And-Trace
criteria.text: Every requirement is singular, verifiable, declaratively tested, with a complete trace chain; no orphans.
criteria.five: every requirement resolves to a pain or gap, a persona, a verbatim quote, a named source, a declarative test and a signal; every bet names its test and the condition under which the alternative wins
criteria.one: the trace-integrity precheck reports an error, a requirement bundles several outcomes, or an acceptance test is not Given/When/Then

criteria.label: Tiers-And-Alternatives
criteria.text: Tiers follow the evidence rule; must-have is rare and defended; alternatives considered are present.
criteria.five: every must-have carries two independent origins and a primary persona in its rationale; rejected alternatives name their trade-off
criteria.one: tiers are typed rather than derived, most requirements are must-have, or no alternative was considered

criteria.label: Success-Signals
criteria.text: Success signals follow the seven-field rule, include leading and lagging, carry guardrails, and invent no figures.
criteria.five: every signal is an observable event with instrument, population, direction, baseline status, type and guardrail with rollback authority; numbers appear only in quotes and typed targets
criteria.one: a signal lacks a field, a baseline is a bare figure, a target is set in the first draft, or any prose carries a naked number

criteria.label: Quality-Accessibility-Privacy
criteria.text: Quality, accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA) and privacy (the regime that governs the subject's jurisdiction and sector, e.g. FERPA for US student records, GDPR only where it applies, plus a privacy impact assessment trigger) are stated as verifiable minimums.
criteria.five: the applicable ISO/IEC 25010 characteristics each carry a verifiable statement (typed target where a bound is needed), the exposed WCAG criteria are named, and the applicable privacy regime is named, and the data-minimization statement and privacy impact assessment trigger check are present
criteria.one: absent, or stated as aspirations with no verifiable statement

criteria.label: Delivery
criteria.text: Delivery is startable and stoppable: states, data touchpoints, dependencies, tracking plan, rollout with kill criteria, open questions with owners and dates, one accountable approver.
criteria.five: every screen lists its required states, every dependency names its owning team, every rollout phase names its gate, kill criteria and rollback authority, and one person is accountable
criteria.one: no rollout, a phase without kill criteria, an open question without owner and date, or no accountable approver

decision: withhold on a 1 for any blocking item; refine when any item is below the floor; pass otherwise

shape.scores: array of ten { n, score, finding }
shape.withheld: true when any item in fail_artifact_on_one scores 1 or any item scores below pass_floor
shape.withheld_reason: string naming the item and the finding

verdict_rule.reader_visibility: none: the verdict is a run record, never prose on the artifact
